correctness.rationale: Every independent d-set of C_{2d} must alternate, so K_d is the join of two (d-2)-sphere boundaries, a simply connected sphere for d>=3. Fixed barycentric point is equivalent to invariant simplex, equivalent to a vertex orbit lying in the downward-closed K_d. Even m=2k fixes some point exactly when gcd(d,k)>1; odd m exactly when gcd(d,m)>1, from parity-block orbit sizes. Armstrong then gives C_{2d}/N. The arithmetic subgroup generators yield C_p for odd prime-power d, C_4 for two-power d and trivial group for mixed-prime d; H1 is the abelianization. Two independent finite enumerations cross-check rotation stabilizers for d=3..100 and quotient barycentric H1 modulo five primes at d=3,4,5. These are corroborations, not all-parameter proof.

value.rationale: The recent topology of bounded-independence spheres naturally raises the topology of their symmetry quotients. Existing rational homology sees a top-dimensional sphere class for all d, but cannot detect any finite first homology. This complete infinite arithmetic classification shows a sharp prime-power versus mixed-prime transition in actual π1, including order-four torsion at every two-power index, giving a structural new invariant for these quotients rather than an arbitrary small computation.
